standard_prerequisites.use: Descent theory's characterization of fpqc coverings as universal effective epimorphic families (Descent, fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms) and Categories' language of cocones; cited inputs with the mapping-property reduction written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Reformulate W = colim X_i as the universal property for maps out of W into any scheme T.
Use effective descent: maps W -> T are the same as maps W_a -> T agreeing on overlaps.
Transfer the colimit property from the local pieces and overlaps to the global cocone.

proof_roadmap.step: Convert the colimit claim into a statement about morphisms out of W.
Apply fpqc effective descent to glue the local universal properties.

difficulty_reason: For a diagram of schemes over S with cocone W, if some fpqc covering {W_a -> W} trivializes the colimit property both for each W_a and for each overlap W_a x_W W_b (as colimits of the base-changed diagram), then W itself is the colimit of the diagram in the category of schemes. The retained proof writes out the decisive reduction: a morphism W -> T out of the cocone is the same thing as a collection of morphisms W_a -> T agreeing on the overlaps W_a x_W W_b, which is exactly the fpqc universal effective epimorphism property of the covering (Descent), so the compatible families indexed by the diagram glue uniquely through W. Retained author proof at lines 4199-4204.
